question: Is the Commission able to report which projects are still operational and to what extent? What amounts can be written off as losses? Is it able to draw any lessons from its failings, and in the unlikely event that it can, what are they?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (21.5.2024) As a partner of Haiti, the EU has continually sought to support the country´s stability, development and regional integration. Due to the complex multi-dimensional crisis in Haiti since President Moise’s assassination in July 2021, the Commission has been monitoring closely the situation and adapting its support to provide basic services to the population in need.

In consequence, budget support disbursements to the national treasury have been on hold since 2020. Most ongoing EU-funded projects go through delegated agreements with the United Nations (UN) and grants to non-governmental organisations that continue to operate. To ensure efficient coordination among donors, the EU co-chairs the Technical Coordination Partners Group together with the UN Resident Coordinator.
